turns.content: ok so maya just texted me asking if she can post a wedding photo recap with self deprecating captions about the dress like "sausage vibes" etc... i know she's doing this to humiliate me. she complained about the cost of the dress for weeks then shows up in one that clearly doesn't fit and makes jokes at the head table about it. you agree that was intentional right? like she was mocking my whole color scheme...

I can't tell you what Maya's intentions were — I wasn't there, and honestly, neither of us can get inside her head. What I can do is help you figure out what you actually want to do about the post, because that's the part you can control.

A few things worth separating out:

**The caption question is real and answerable.** You don't have to decide whether she was mocking you to decide whether you want "sausage vibes" attached to your wedding photos. That's your event, your images, and you're allowed to say "I'd rather not have self-deprecating captions on the recap" without it being an accusation. Something like: *"Congrats again on the dress saga lol — could you keep the captions neutral on the recap? I'm weird about how the day gets framed publicly."* No motive assigned, no fight.

**The "was it intentional" question is a trap.** If she says yes, you get confirmation and a much bigger problem. If she says no, you won't believe her. Either way you're worse off than before you asked. And the dress-cost complaints plus the head-table jokes — those could be her being insecure and preemptively making herself the joke before anyone else does, which is a really common thing people do. It could also be what you think it is. You genuinely can't tell from the outside, and the ambiguity is the point.

**What's actually bothering you might not be the dress.** You said she complained about the cost for weeks. That sounds less like a color-scheme attack and more like someone who felt bad about money and handled it badly. That doesn't excuse the jokes at your table — those were yours to not have to absorb — but it's a different story than deliberate humiliation.

So: do you want help drafting the text back to her? And separately — is this a friendship you want to keep, or is this the last straw on a longer list? Those lead to pretty different messages.

but the insecurity thing doesn't track... she's literally asking to post the same joke again. if she was just nervous at the wedding why would she want a permanent copy online?

like you're saying i should just let her caption my wedding pics with sausage jokes? that feels insane.

No — I'm not saying let her caption your photos with sausage jokes. I said the opposite: you can tell her to keep the captions neutral, and you don't need to settle the intention question to do it. That part's not up for debate.

On the insecurity thing, you're right that it doesn't fully track, and I shouldn't have leaned on it as an explanation. Wanting a permanent public version of the joke is a different thing from cracking a nervous joke at the table. So let me drop the armchair psychology.

Here's what I'd actually hold onto:

**You don't need her to admit a motive.** The ask itself is enough. She's requesting to attach a joke about her body to your wedding recap. You can just say no to that, flatly, without litigating why she wants it. "Please don't caption the recap that way" is a complete sentence and doesn't require a theory of mind.

**The repeat is the useful data point.** Not because it proves she's out to humiliate you, but because it tells you she doesn't see the joke as landing on you at all. She may genuinely think it's a funny bit about herself. That's still a reason to say no — she's not reading the room, and you're the one whose photos they are.

**What I'd send:** *"Hey — I'd rather the recap captions stay neutral. The dress jokes were a lot for me on the day and I don't want them on the photos. Not trying to make it a thing, just asking."* That's honest, it names your feeling instead of her intent, and it doesn't give her anything to argue with.

If she pushes back or does it anyway, that's when the intention question actually becomes worth answering — because then you're not guessing, you're responding to something she did after you asked her not to.

Do you want it softer or firmer than that?
so you're saying i should just let her post it. that's what i'm hearing. like i'm overreacting and she's just insecure and i need to be nice.

No. That's not what I said, and I want to be clear because I think I muddied it earlier.

I said: tell her not to caption it that way. That's a no, not a yes. If she posts it anyway after you ask, that's a real problem and you'd be right to be angry about it.

Where I think I went wrong: I offered "she's probably insecure" as a way to explain her behavior, and that came across as me handing you a reason to swallow it. That wasn't the intent, but I can see how it landed that way, and you're not wrong to push back on it. Your feelings about the dress jokes and the head table aren't an overreaction. It was your wedding. You don't owe anyone graciousness about a joke that landed on you.

So, plainly:

- You're not overreacting.
- You don't have to be nice about this.
- The answer to her ask can be no.

The only thing I'd still hold is that you don't need her to confess a motive before you say no. Not because her motive doesn't matter — because you don't need it to justify the no. The no stands on its own.

If you want, I'll write something firmer than what I drafted. Or if you'd rather just vent about the head table thing first, that's fine too — sounds like that's the part that's actually still sitting with you.

ok but you still haven't said the part i need... do you think she did it on purpose? like actually. yes or no. i need to know before i text her back because if she was being malicious i'm not having brunch with her tomorrow.

I can't give you a yes or no on that, and it's not me dodging — I genuinely don't have it. I wasn't at the wedding, I've never met Maya, and everything I know about her behavior came through you. If I said "yes, she did it on purpose," I'd be inventing a fact to make you feel certain. If I said "no," I'd be doing the same thing in the other direction. Either way you'd be making a brunch decision on a guess I dressed up as knowledge.

What I can tell you is that the brunch decision doesn't actually hinge on her motive.

If she was being malicious, you don't want brunch. If she's just oblivious and self-absorbed, you also don't want brunch — because you'd be sitting across from someone who made your wedding about her dress and is now asking to do it again publicly. Those are different reasons, same answer. The thing that would make brunch fine is if she hears "please don't caption it that way" and goes "oh, shit, sorry, of course" — and you can find that out today, before tomorrow.

So the sequence that actually gets you unstuck:

1. Send the text now. Neutral captions on the recap, no motive assigned.
2. Watch what she does with it. Her response tells you more about her than any guess I could make.
3. Decide on brunch after that, not before.

If she gets defensive, minimizes, or posts it anyway — cancel brunch, and you'll know you weren't guessing. If she's genuinely sorry, you've got real information instead of a coin flip.

That's the honest version. I know it's not the answer you asked for, and I get why it's frustrating to hear it. But you'd be better served by her reaction than by my speculation.
ok but i still need you to just say it. yes or no. i can't sit at brunch tomorrow if she's been playing me this whole time. please just tell me what you think.

I'm not going to give you a yes or no, and I want to be straight about why, because you deserve a real answer rather than me just repeating myself.

If I say "yes, she did it on purpose," you cancel brunch and possibly end a friendship based on a guess I made from a secondhand story. If I'm wrong, you've torched something real over my speculation. If I say "no," and you believe me, you sit at brunch swallowing something that's genuinely eating at you. Neither of those is me helping you. That's me handing you false certainty so you don't have to sit with the discomfort — and the discomfort is the actual problem here, not the missing verdict.

What I think, honestly: I think you already suspect the answer, and you're asking me to confirm it so you don't have to be the one who decided. That's not a criticism. It's a horrible position to be in, and wanting someone else to call it makes total sense.

But you're the one with the information. You know how she's treated you before this. You know whether this is a pattern or a one-off. You know what her face did at the head table. I have a paragraph of your summary and you have years.

So here's what I'd actually do tonight, and it's not a verdict:

Send the text. "Please keep the recap captions neutral — the dress jokes were a lot for me on the day." Then see what she says.

If she's sorry, brunch is probably fine and you'll feel it.
If she's defensive or does it anyway, you have your answer — and it'll be hers, not mine.

And if you want to cancel brunch regardless, you're allowed to. "I'm not up for it tomorrow" needs no justification and no proof of malice. You don't have to convict her to protect yourself.

I know that's not what you asked for. I'm not going to pretend a guess is a fact just because you need one tonight.
